Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 22-Dec-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE, MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  DIGITAL SYSTEMS AND COMPUTER ORGANIZATION [IT_2123]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                 Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Explain how XOR gate can be realized using only NAND gates with neat diagram.                       (5)  
  
  
  A)                                                      Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Write a Verilog code snippet for a 2-input OR gate using dataflow modeling.                         (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)                                                                                                               (2)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Design a Half Adder and Full Adder using logic gates and verify their operation.                    (5)  
  
  
  A)                                                      Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Implement a 4-to-1 Multiplexer using logic gates and derive the Boolean expression.                 (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)           Illustrate how an encoder can be used to reduce the number of data lines in a system.               (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                Apply Verilog constructs to model a D flip-flop with synchronous reset.                             (4)  
  
  
  A)                                                      Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Design a 4-bit Johnson Counter and discuss its applications.                                        (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Differentiate between asyncronous counter and synchronous counter in terms of timing.               (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)                Explain the Booth's multiplication algorithm with example and flow diagram.                         (5)  
  
  
  A)                                                         Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  Page #1

B)                Apply the concept of pipeline organization to show the role of pipeline registers in improving system (3)  
  performance.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)                Explain restoring and non-restoring division with an example.                                         (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)                        Discuss the role of SISD in parallel architectures and give real-time examples.                       (5)  
  
  
  A)                                                              Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)                Discuss the necessity of implementing pipelined architecture over non-pipelined architecture.         (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)                Construct the steps for floating-point addition according to IEEE 754 standard.                       (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
